description_full: Southern Copper Corporation engages in mining, exploring, smelting, and refining copper and other minerals in Mexico, the United States, Peru, Brazil, Chile, and Other American countries. The company is involved in the mining, milling, and flotation of copper ore to produce copper and molybdenum concentrates; smelting of copper concentrates to produce blister and anode copper; refining of anode copper to produce copper cathodes; production of copper-molybdenum concentrates and sulfuric acid; production of refined silver, gold, and other materials; and mining and processing of copper, molybdenum, zinc, silver, gold and lead. It operates the Toquepala and Cuajone open-pit mines, smelter, and refinery in Peru; La Caridad, an open-pit copper mine, as well as copper ore concentrator; and SX-EW plant, a smelter, refinery, and rod plant in Mexico. The company also operates Buenavista, an open-pit copper mine, as well as copper concentrators and operating SX-EW plants in Mexico. In addition, it operates underground mines that produce zinc, lead, copper, silver, and gold; coal mine; and zinc refinery. The company has interests in 164,805 hectares and 505,788 hectares of concessions in Peru and Mexico; and 98,634 hectares and 28,453 hectares of exploration concessions in Argentina and Chile. Southern Copper Corporation was formerly known as Southern Peru Copper Corp. and changed its name to Southern Copper Corporation in July 1996. The company was incorporated in 1952 and is based in Phoenix, Arizona. Southern Copper Corporation operates as a subsidiary of Americas Mining Corporation.

financial_summary: Southern Copper Corporation is a large-cap basic materials business with a $140.0B market cap on $13.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +10% over the past three years and +10% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 29% against a 10% cost of capital — a 20-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 42%.

The business throws off $3.4B in free cash flow — roughly 26 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.10× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.2× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 18× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 1.8%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 89% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 4.0× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
